facts.text: I'm Dhruv Mishra, a software engineer at Microsoft in Noida, India. I build production AI agents and the Azure backend services they run on. I studied Computer Science and Applied Mathematics at IIIT Delhi and I'm a Codeforces Expert. Outside work I'm into the gym, chess, PC overclocking, and longevity research.

This portfolio is a sketchbook-themed site built with Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind v4, and Framer Motion. It has a live voice agent you can interrupt mid-sentence, a RAG chatbot with 5 selectable LLMs, a retro terminal, a guestbook, and unlockable stickers. It ships as Docker images through GitHub Actions to Linux VMs on Azure, GCP, and Oracle Cloud, behind Nginx and Cloudflare. Everything is free except the domain.

Favorite language is C++. Day to day I write C#, TypeScript, Python, Kotlin, C++, Java, JavaScript, and SQL. On the AI side I work with LLM agents, multi-agent systems, MCP, tool calling, RAG, embeddings, LLM evaluation, voice agents (speech-to-text and text-to-speech), speculative decoding, and quantized local models on llama.cpp, plus classical ML like XGBoost. Backend and cloud: Azure (Service Fabric, VM Scale Sets, Cosmos DB), Redis, Node.js, REST APIs, Docker, Nginx, Linux, Cloudflare, GCP, and OCI. Frontend and mobile: React, Next.js, Vue, Electron, Tailwind, and Android with Jetpack Compose. Tooling: Git, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Kusto, CI/CD, and observability.

Current role: Software Engineer at Microsoft since June 2024, based in Noida, India. I build production AI agents and the Azure backend services they run on. The main pieces are LLM incident-triage agents that use MCP tools and cut manual on-call triage by 40%, a $240k-a-year Azure cost cut on a backend serving more than 7 billion requests a day, sandboxed PDF encryption in Office for the web, faster Office Android startup, and maintaining Fluent UI Android.

Favorite games: Witcher 3, Metal Gear Solid V, and the Horizon games (Zero Dawn and Forbidden West). Reached Immortal 2 rank in Valorant. I also play modded Minecraft with friends on an Azure-hosted server I set up and maintain myself.

Main hobbies: gym and strength training, chess, gaming, travel, PC hardware overclocking, and following longevity research. Outside of code I like going deep on whatever I'm currently interested in — whether that's memory timings, a particular game, or a nutrition protocol.

Based in India. Traveled to the EU, Singapore, Vietnam, many places across India, and the US including Las Vegas, Los Angeles, New York City, and Seattle.

AtomVault — a secure, ACID-compliant banking database built for high-reliability transactions. Features full transaction rollback and recovery, multi-user architecture, and strict role-based access control with admin, teller, and customer roles. Stack: Java, MySQL, JDBC, OOP, ACID Compliance. Year: 2022, 2 months. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/AtomVault.

Relaxed Concurrent Counting Bloom Filters, my undergraduate research at IIIT Delhi's Distributed Computing Lab under Prof. Bapi Chatterjee. I built a lock-free C++ Counting Bloom Filter that uses relaxed synchronization to get 3x the throughput of the baseline under high contention, with little effect on false positive and false negative rates. It was benchmarked against existing concurrent filter implementations and published in the IIIT Delhi repository. Stack: C++, Bloom Filters, Concurrency, Optimization, Data Structures. Year: 2024, 8 months. Link: repository.iiitd.edu.in/jspui/handle/123456789/1613.

Course Similarity Evaluator — an intelligent Python tool designed to detect redundant course content across university curriculums. Built a fuzzy matching pipeline with text similarity algorithms over course syllabi, identifying redundant modules with configurable similarity thresholds so students can avoid retaking equivalent coursework. Originally an engineering project at IIIT Delhi under Prof. Dhruv Kumar. Stack: Python, Fuzzy Logic, NLP, Data Analysis, Algorithm Design, scikit-learn. Year: 2023, 2 months. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/Course-Similarity-Evaluator.

Cropio is my privacy-conscious AI portrait cropper that turns raw photos into polished headshots. Live at cropio.whoisdhruv.com. Architecture: Next.js + TypeScript frontend with a Python FastAPI backend. Uses YOLO11 pose estimation plus face-orientation detection to capture different angles of the face and generate multiple headshot crop suggestions, with deterministic geometry fallbacks, an interactive drag-resize editor with aspect-ratio presets, and full-resolution browser exports. Image descriptions are generated via NVIDIA multimodal LLM APIs and indexed locally in vector IndexedDB for semantic session search over saved crops — no server-side image storage, everything stays in the browser. Supports full local session management. Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, FastAPI, YOLO11 Pose, IndexedDB, NVIDIA APIs, OpenCV, Python. Year: 2026, ongoing. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/Cropio-ImageEditor.

Fluent UI Android is the official Microsoft native Android library enabling developers to build uniform Microsoft 365 experiences. I managed its release lifecycle as sole owner across 10 releases for 10+ partner teams including Copilot, Office, Outlook, OneDrive, and Teams. The library is Kotlin/Java with Jetpack Compose, XML layouts, Gradle/Maven builds, official Fluent design tokens, typography styles, and custom controls for the Microsoft ecosystem. Stack: Kotlin, Java, Android SDK, Jetpack Compose, XML, Gradle, Maven, Design Systems, API Design. Repo: github.com/microsoft/fluentui-android.

Hybrid Entertainment Recommender — a context-aware movie recommendation system that integrates collaborative, content-based, and demographic filtering to solve the cold-start problem and personalize content for diverse user groups. Stack: Python, scikit-learn, Pandas, SVD, TensorFlow, Recommendation Systems. Year: 2023, 3 months. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/Age-and-Context-Sensitive-Hybrid-Entertaintment-Recommender-System.

Invoke is an open-source Windows voice assistant I built for running coding agents by voice. It answers simple requests itself and hands bigger coding and research tasks to GitHub Copilot CLI agents, each coding task in its own Git worktree, so several can run in parallel without stepping on each other. Speech-to-text, the language model, and text-to-speech can all run locally: NVIDIA Parakeet for speech recognition, quantized Gemma or Qwen models on llama.cpp, and Kokoro for speech. Speculative decoding with a draft model plus thread tuning made local generation 35% faster, and a benchmark harness I wrote picked a speech model with 57% fewer errors than Whisper Small at 5x the speed. It also keeps tasks, follow-ups, notifications, and files in one place, and ships as a Windows installer with an in-app updater. Stack: Electron, Node.js, Python, llama.cpp, MCP. Year: 2026, ongoing. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/Invoke-Voice.

Instant Vital Checkup (IVC) — a contactless, computer-vision-powered health screening kiosk that automates patient triage. Using OpenCV and MediaPipe in a real-time pipeline, it calculates height, weight, BMI, and pulse from a single camera at a distance, drastically reducing wait times. Stack: Python, OpenCV, MediaPipe, Computer Vision, HealthTech, Real-time Processing. Year: 2023, 4 months. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/Instant-Vital-Checkup-IVC.

Jarvis is a voice AI dispatch agent I built for a demo logistics app (Dhruv FreightOps). You place a call and talk to it: it looks up loads, assigns carriers, negotiates freight rates, submits quotes, schedules callbacks, and moves around the app for you. It uses an LLM planner with MCP tools and RAG over load and carrier data, and it acts on the page through tool calls. It's a personal side project I built on my own time. It is NOT a Microsoft product and is not affiliated with my employer's work. Live demo at jarvis.whoisdhruv.com (anyone can try it). Source code is public at github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/AudioControlledAgenticWebsite. Architecture: a vanilla HTML/CSS/JS frontend with an AudioWorklet capturing 16 kHz PCM, and a Node.js backend that bridges a long-lived WebSocket to a live voice model. The UX follows a phone call: Place Call and End Call, optional call-center background noise, phone-line band-pass filtering, five personas, barge-in, and native voice activity detection. The WebSocket, AudioContext, and microphone live in one long-lived page shell, so the call doesn't drop when you move between pages. No audio is uploaded until the call starts, context is compressed with a sliding window at 80k tokens, and the system prompt and tool schemas stay stable so prompt caching works. Stack: JavaScript, Node.js, WebSockets, AudioWorklet, MCP, RAG, Tool Calling. Year: 2026, ongoing. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/AudioControlledAgenticWebsite. Live demo: jarvis.whoisdhruv.com.

This portfolio website, whoisdhruv.com. It's a server-rendered Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind v4 site with a hand-drawn sketchbook look (pencil cursor, paper textures, tape strips). Everything is free except the domain. Stack: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Gemini Live, RAG, Docker, GitHub Actions, Nginx, Cloudflare. Year: 2025, ongoing. Repo: github.com/Dhruv-Mishra/portfolioWebsite.

The site features a full AI chat page (/chat) designed around a sticky note desk interface. Visitors can ask me questions — I answer in first person with short sticky-note-style replies. The chat can also trigger UI actions like opening projects, switching themes, or jumping to pages when the user explicitly asks.

The about page (/about) includes an interactive experience timeline populated with Dhruv's real career data. It covers his current Software Engineer role at Microsoft, where he builds production AI agents and the Azure backend services they run on; his Machine Learning Engineer role at growIndigo; his Microsoft Loop software engineering internship; IIIT Delhi CSAM education; DCLL research; and competitive programming / award highlights. The timeline supports filtering by work, internship, research, education, and awards, and expands each entry into impact, highlights, location, dates, and tools.

The guestbook at /guestbook is a sticky-note wall where visitors can pin a short signed note. Each note rotates at a random small angle, cycles through the site's note color palette (yellow, blue, green, purple, orange), and shows up live on the wall. Name and message are length-capped and signing the guestbook unlocks the "Left a Mark" sticker.

The Escape the Matrix puzzle is a multi-stage hidden challenge woven across Dhruv's site, primarily driven through the home page terminal. The full stage enum lives in `lib/matrixPuzzle.ts` and currently spans nine stages from first contact through final escape.

High-level stage progression (no spoilers on specific values):
1. The visitor starts by collecting stickers. Every interactive surface on the site earns one, and the sticker drawer at `/stickers` tracks progress.
2. Once every visible sticker is earned, the `sudo` prefix unlocks in the home terminal. Before that point, any `sudo <cmd>` invocation is politely denied.
3. With sudo unlocked, the visitor explores hidden files via `sudo ls` and `sudo cat <file>`. One of those files contains the credentials needed for the next stage.
4. The contents of that hidden file are used to log into `sudo admin`, which gates the experimental commands toggle.
5. Flipping the experimental commands toggle inside the admin surface enables the `sudo matrix` command path.
6. Running `sudo matrix` (with the required two-step `yes` confirmation) engages the persistent matrix-rain overlay and triggers the disco-mode timer phase.
7. The visitor waits through the timer while the overlay builds up.
8. Finally, an "ESCAPE THE MATRIX" button fades into the overlay. Clicking it completes the puzzle.
9. The post-escape reward is the `/matrix-notes` page, which is only reachable after escaping.

Canonical help mechanism: typing `matrix hint` in the home terminal returns a stage-appropriate nudge for whichever stage the visitor is currently on. This is the intended way for a stuck visitor to ask for help. Hints are deliberately oblique rather than step-by-step, but they do change as the visitor progresses, so re-running `matrix hint` after each milestone surfaces the next pointer.

The full chain is intentionally non-linear and non-obvious. Specific passwords, the exact admin credentials, the contents of the hidden file, and the precise click sequence are all puzzle content. The chat agent should never spoil any of those values directly. When a visitor asks for help with the puzzle in chat, the right move is to point them at the home terminal's `matrix hint` command and encourage them to run it from whichever stage they're currently stuck on.

The matrix overlay engaged by `sudo matrix` is a one-way trip until escape: it persists across page navigation and browser refreshes, and the only dismissal path is the on-overlay button (first the glowing "WAKE UP" appears, and after the puzzle's terminal phase completes the "ESCAPE THE MATRIX" button replaces it).

Site pages: home with an interactive retro terminal (/), about with an interactive experience timeline (/about), projects (/projects), resume (/resume), chat (/chat), guestbook (/guestbook), and stickers (/stickers). The home page features the terminal as the entry point and a Talk to me note that starts native voice mode on the current route; the about page shows Dhruv's career timeline; the chat page hosts the full AI chat; the guestbook lets visitors sign the wall; the stickers page displays the achievement album.

Keyboard shortcuts: navigation uses `g`-chord sequences — g then h for home, g p for projects, g a for about, g r for resume, g c for chat, g b for guestbook, g s for stickers. The chord window is 1.2 seconds. Actions: `t` toggles the theme, `?` opens the shortcuts overlay on desktop, `Esc` closes overlays. Shortcuts do not intercept typing in editable fields or system modifier keys.

The site has 11 regular unlockable stickers earned by exploring, plus a hidden completion award ("Superuser") for completionists who collect all 11. Every sticker is reachable on touch devices — nothing is keyboard-only. The 11 regular stickers in STICKER_ROSTER are: "The First Word" (type your first terminal command), "Lights On, Lights Off" (toggle the theme between day and night), "Pen Pal" (send a note via feedback), "The Whole Tour" (visit every page on the site), "Serious Chat" (have a real chat on the chat page), "Left a Mark" (pin a note to the guestbook), "Case Files" (open a project note on /projects), "Chat Conductor" (ask the AI chat to perform an action), "Repo Hunter" (follow a project back to its source repo), "Social Butterfly" (tap one of the social sidebar links), and "Phoned a Friend" (call the website voice agent). Browse unlocked stickers at /stickers. Hardcore collectors who collect all 11 regular stickers automatically unlock the hidden completion award: "Superuser".

The home terminal accepts real commands: help, about, projects, contact, socials, ls, cat [file], open [file], clear, joke, skills, resume, cv, chat, feedback, guestbook, sign, stickers, cheatsheet, disco, sudo [cmd], init, whoami, date, github, and linkedin. `ls` lists fake files such as about.md, projects.json, cropio.md, resume.pdf, contact.txt, and secrets.env. `cat` reads available files, `open resume.pdf` opens the resume page, and `joke` uses JokeAPI.

Site interactions have lightweight, procedurally synthesized Web Audio sounds for page turns, chat, stickers, themes, terminal input, and modals. A sitewide speaker toggle mutes those sounds plus disco and Matrix music. It respects browser autoplay rules and quiets when the tab is hidden.

`sudo` commands are denied until the visitor earns every sticker. After root unlock, `sudo help` lists hidden commands and `sudo cheatsheet` shows sticker progress. Hidden commands include `sudo matrix`, `sudo rainbow`, `sudo fortune`, `sudo whoami`, and destructive `sudo reset yes`. The exact unlock trigger remains for visitors to discover.

`disco`, `disco yes`, `disco no`, and `disco off` are public commands. `disco` and `sudo matrix` require a second confirmation with `yes`; `no` aborts. Matrix mode persists across navigation and refresh, and only its on-screen `WAKE UP` or later escape button can dismiss it. Disco exits through `disco off` and stays dark.

The site's visual idiom is a hand-drawn sketchbook: paper textures, torn-tape strips, thumbtacks, ruled-line backgrounds, folded-corner notes, a custom pencil/chalk cursor that leaves a short trail, and the hand-drawn `font-hand` alongside monospace for code. Everything supports light and dark themes; dark mode keeps the sketchbook feel with warmer inks on darker paper.
